transcript.content: Hello, how are you doing today? What brings you in to see me?

I’m doing okay, I guess. Not terrible. Mostly I came in because I’ve just been… tired, in a way that doesn’t really add up. I can sleep and I’m still keeping up at work, so it’s not like I’m falling apart or anything, but I feel like I’m running on a low battery before the day even really gets started, if that makes sense.
How long have you been feeling this way, and does it happen most days?

It’s been a while, honestly. I’d say it really started when I got pulled back into full operational leadership at work… about two years and four months ago. And yes, I mean, most days it’s there, though I try not to make too much of it.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that activities you once found pleasurable feel less rewarding now?

Yeah… I suppose so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I still do things, but for a long time now there’s been this kind of gray, flat feeling most days.

Like fishing, or working on the tomatoes, or going to a church concert—those are things I used to really look forward to. Lately they can feel more like something I’m checking off a list than something I’m actually enjoying. Does that make sense?
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or like you're not measuring up to expectations lately, even when there's no clear reason for it?

I don’t think so… not in any big way. I mean, I probably hold myself to a pretty high standard, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been sitting around feeling guilty for no reason. At least, not that I’ve really noticed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus, make decisions, or think clearly lately?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed anything major there. I mean, I still get through my work and make decisions when I need to. Maybe I have the normal moments where I have to reread an email or think something over a little longer, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it.

Nothing that’s really stood out to me as a big problem, I guess. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking about?
Have you noticed that you move more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, that you feel restless or fidgety without meaning to?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’m probably not moving as fast as I did when I was younger, but I haven’t noticed anything like… dramatically slowed down or like I can’t sit still.

Maybe I shift around a little if I’m bored, but nothing that seems out of the ordinary to me. Is that helpful?
Have you noticed a loss of energy or increased fatigue, even after resting or sleeping?

Yeah… that’s probably the main thing, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I’m still getting to work and doing what I need to do, but I do feel tired in a way that doesn’t quite add up.

Like, I can sleep and still wake up feeling like I’m already on a low battery before the day really starts. That’s part of why I came in, I guess. Does that make sense?
Have you ever felt like life isn’t worth living, or had thoughts about harming yourself, even if you wouldn’t act on them?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I feel worn down or discouraged, sure, but not like I’m thinking of hurting myself or that life isn’t worth living.

I wouldn’t want you to worry about that. If that’s what you’re asking, I don’t really have those thoughts.
Have you found yourself feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for a period of time lasting most of the day?

Yeah… I guess I would say yes, though I don’t like to make it sound worse than it is.

It’s more like this gray, flat feeling that’s been there most days for a long time. Not like I’m crying all day or anything, but things I used to look forward to—fishing, working on the tomatoes, even a church concert—can feel more like something I’m checking off a list than really enjoying.

I’m not sure if that’s what you mean by depressed, but… that’s probably fair to say.
